TL-RGPD-APP: The regulation becomes applicable across the Union, without any transposition measure.
TL-PUB-333: Both texts appear on the same day in Official Journal L 333. This is no coincidence: they form a joined-up set-up, in which DORA is the financial lex specialis of NIS2.
TL-NIS2-VIG: Twentieth day after publication. The twenty-one-month transposition period starts running.
TL-DORA-RTS1: First package of DORA technical standards
Delegated Regulations 2024/1774 (ICT risk management framework) and 2024/1772 (incident classification). They are what make Articles 15 and 18 operational.
TL-NIS2-TRANSPO: Deadline for adopting national provisions. France missed it: as of 22 September 2026, the resilience bill has still not been enacted.
TL-NIS2-EXEC: Quantified technical requirements and significant incident criteria for digital providers: DNS, domain name registries, cloud computing, data centres, content delivery networks, managed and managed security services, online marketplaces, search engines, social networks, trust services. For these players, case-by-case assessment gives way to thresholds.
TL-DORA-ITS-REG: Register of information templates, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956
Fifteen table templates linked by identifiers, setting the exact structure of the register to be submitted annually.
TL-DORA-APP: The regulation becomes applicable to financial entities. No transitional period was granted: obligations are fully enforceable from this date.
TL-NIS2-A27: Deadline by which digital providers had to submit their identification information to the competent authorities, for the register kept by ENISA.
TL-NIS2-LISTE: National lists of essential and important entities drawn up
Date by which Member States had to draw up the list of their essential and important entities, then review it at least every two years.
TL-ENISA-GUIDE: One hundred and seventy pages translating Implementing Regulation 2024/2690 into operational measures and examples of expected evidence. The de facto reference for inspections.
TL-DORA-TLPT: Technical standards on threat-led testing enter into force
Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190, aligned with the TIBER-EU methodology.
TL-DORA-SOUSTRAIT: Technical standards on subcontracting enter into force
Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/532: what the financial entity must establish before authorising a subcontracting chain: visibility of further subcontractors, concentration risk, data location.
TL-DORA-CTPP: First nineteen critical third-party providers designated
For the first time, the European supervisory authorities place cloud, data centre, telecommunications and software providers under direct European oversight.
TL-OMNIBUS: The Commission proposes amending the GDPR, the ePrivacy Directive, NIS2 and DORA. The artificial intelligence part was adopted by the Council on 29 June 2026; the data part is still under negotiation.
TL-EDPB-AVIS: Joint Opinion 2/2026 of the EDPB and EDPS
Official position of the European data protection authorities on the Digital Omnibus. A marker of the ongoing debate on the definition of personal data and the consent regime.
TL-RECYF: ANSSI publishes the Référentiel Cyber France: twenty security objectives and one hundred and fifty-two acceptable means of compliance, with separate applicability for important and essential entities. A working document, but today the most operational reading grid for NIS2 in France.
TL-DORA-SUPERV: Lead overseers take up their duties
Each critical third-party provider is assigned a lead overseer, assisted by joint examination teams, who carries out risk assessments and adopts annual and multi-year oversight plans.
TL-CRA-PUB: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 enters into force twenty days after publication. It then applies in stages, until 11 December 2027.
TL-CRA-DESC: Technical description of important and critical products

Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392 enters into force, specifying the twenty-eight categories of Annexes III and IV. It determines, product by product, whether self-assessment is enough or a third party must be involved.
TL-CRA-ONEC: Chapter IV becomes applicable: Member States notify the bodies authorised to assess product conformity. In France, ANSSI is the notifying authority.
TL-CRA-ART14: Article 14 applies: every manufacturer reports actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through ENISA's single platform, with an early warning within 24 hours and a notification within 72 hours. The obligation also covers products already on the market.
TL-FR-AN: Resilience bill debated in the National Assembly

The conference of presidents of 22 September 2026 put the bill transposing NIS2 on the public session agenda from 7 October. It is the first concrete signal of an enforceable compliance timetable in France.
TL-CRA-FULL: Essential requirements, conformity assessment, CE marking and the obligations of importers and distributors become enforceable. A non-compliant product can no longer be placed on the Union market.
TL-FR-LOI: Expected enactment of the resilience act

The bill on the resilience of critical infrastructure and strengthening cybersecurity transposes NIS2 and DORA's accompanying directive. After the public session debate opening on 7 October, the shuttle between chambers, implementing decrees and the final ReCyF will follow. Indicative date.
TL-NIS2-REEXAM: First biennial review of national lists
Member States review and update the list of essential and important entities at least every two years.
TL-AI-VIG: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Official Journal of 12 July 2024. It then applies in stages.
TL-AI-INTERDIT: Chapters I and II apply: Article 5 practices are prohibited and providers and deployers must build their staff's AI literacy.
TL-AI-GPAI: The obligations of general-purpose AI model providers, European governance and the penalty regime become applicable.
TL-AI-OMNIBUS: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 postpones the obligations for high-risk systems, relaxes the AI literacy obligation and extends SME relief to small mid-cap companies.
TL-AI-APP: The regulation becomes applicable, notably the Article 50 transparency obligations: disclosure of interaction with an AI, marking of generated content, labelling of deepfakes.
Provider or deployer of AI systems
TL-AI-OMNI-DEC: New prohibition and end of the marking grace period
Ban on systems generating child sexual abuse material or non-consensual intimate content, and end of the grace period granted to systems already on the market to mark the content they generate.
Provider or deployer of AI systems
TL-AI-HR3: Date postponed by the AI Omnibus: risk management, data governance, technical documentation, human oversight, conformity assessment and deployer obligations become enforceable for the Annex III areas.
TL-AI-HR1: Date postponed by the AI Omnibus for AI systems that are safety components of products covered by the Annex I harmonisation legislation: machinery, toys, medical devices, lifts.
Safety component of a regulated product

DUTY-DORA-REGISTRE: Submission of the register of information
The register of all ICT contractual arrangements is submitted to the competent authority at least once a year, using the templates of Implementing Regulation 2024/2956.
DUTY-DORA-TESTS: Testing of systems supporting critical functions
All ICT systems supporting critical or important functions are tested at least once a year.
DUTY-DORA-TLPT: Entities identified by the authority carry out an advanced test at least every three years, on a scope validated upstream and attested downstream.
DUTY-DORA-CADRE: Review of the ICT risk management framework
Annual, and after each major incident
The framework is reviewed at least annually, after each major incident, and following recommendations from audits and prudential supervision.
DUTY-NIS2-PSSI: Review of the security policy and the list of systems
The ReCyF requires an annual review of the security policy (2.B.4) and an annual validation of the inventory of activities and systems (1.3).
DUTY-NIS2-HABILIT: Review of accounts, access rights and filtering rules
The ReCyF requires an annual review of accounts (10.A.6), access rights (10.C.4), filtering rules (7.B.5) and, for essential entities, the configuration of directories and resources (11.B.6, 18.4).
DUTY-NIS2-SAUV: Backup and restoration processes are tested at least once a year, to check that backups are properly made and can actually be restored.
DUTY-NIS2-RISQUE: Every three years, and after an incident
Essential entities review their risk analysis at least every three years, and after an incident or major change in context.
DUTY-NIS2-EXERCICE: Essential entities break their training strategy down into a three-year programme specifying the frequency, nature and objectives of exercises.
DUTY-RGPD-REGISTRE: Update of the record of processing
The record is kept up to date at all times and made available to the supervisory authority on request.
DUTY-CRA-SUPPORT: Each product receives security updates throughout its support period, of at least five years, and the end date is displayed at the time of purchase.
DUTY-AI-INVENTAIRE: Review of the inventory and classification of AI systems
Each new system, substantial modification or change of purpose triggers a review of the classification and of prohibited practices.
DUTY-AI-JOURNAUX: Automatically generated logs are kept for at least six months by the provider and the deployer, for the part under their control.
